title: Aurora Ledger
subtitle: Double-entry accounting engine for multi-currency payments
description:
A ledger service handling settlement across fourteen currencies, built to guarantee that every transaction balances to zero even under partial failure.

The problem

The existing system reconciled overnight in a batch job. A failed payout could sit mis-stated for eighteen hours, and finance caught the drift by hand.

What I built

  • An append-only ledger with idempotent transaction posting
  • Deterministic replay from the event log for audits
  • A reconciliation service that closes the books continuously

Reconciliation lag dropped from ~18 hours to under 400ms at p99.

title: Signal Atlas
subtitle: Real-time observability for edge deployments
description:
A telemetry pipeline collecting metrics from roughly 3,000 edge nodes on intermittent connections, where the usual push-based agents simply stop working.

Approach

Nodes buffer locally and reconcile on reconnect, so a device offline for a week still produces a gap-free time series once it comes back.

  • Store-and-forward agent written in Rust
  • Backfill-aware ingestion that repairs out-of-order windows
  • Query layer serving dashboards over a columnar store

title: Quiet Hours
subtitle: A focus timer that respects your calendar
description:
A small macOS menu-bar app that reads your calendar and blocks notifications during deep-work blocks — without needing an account or sending anything to a server.

Everything runs locally. The whole app is about 4MB.

title: Meridian
subtitle: Design system and component library for a 40-person product org
description:
Consolidated four divergent component libraries into one system, then migrated eleven applications onto it without freezing feature work.

Outcome

  • Component duplication fell from 340 components to 92
  • Accessibility violations dropped 87% against automated audits
  • New-screen build time roughly halved

The hard part was never the components — it was the migration path that let teams adopt it incrementally.
